name: E-Commerce Defective Smartphone Refund Denial
raw_input: I ordered a Samsung Galaxy smartphone worth Rs 26,999 on an e-commerce app on 10th November 2024. It was delivered on 14th November. Within 24 hours of opening the box, the screen started flickering with green lines and touch stopped working. I raised a replacement request on 15th November. The app sent a technician for inspection on 21st November. The technician confirmed it is a manufacturing hardware defect and took sign on his job sheet. But on 23rd November, customer support cancelled my return request stating 'The 7-day return window expired on 21st November'. They are telling me to go to an authorized brand service center 40 km away. I paid for a brand new working phone, not a defective phone repaired on day one. I have the invoice, delivery receipt, technician inspection job sheet copy, and chat screenshots.

case_dossier.case_title: Defective Smartphone Delivery & Arbitrary Rejection of Replacement by E-Commerce App
case_dossier.summary: The user purchased a Samsung Galaxy smartphone for Rs 26,999, which arrived with a manufacturing defect. Although a technician verified the defect within the return window, customer support cancelled the replacement request based on an arbitrary expiry date and refused a refund.

timeline.event: User ordered a Samsung Galaxy smartphone worth Rs 26,999 on the e-commerce app.
Phone was delivered to the user.
Within 24 hours of opening the box, screen started flickering and touch stopped working; user raised a replacement request.
E-commerce app technician inspected the phone, confirmed the manufacturing hardware defect, and took a signature on his job sheet.
Customer support cancelled the return request stating the 7-day return window expired on 21st November and directed the user to an authorized service center.

evidence_needed: Written service center report or job card if visited
Email trail or communication logs with the seller
case_dossier.evidence_strength_explanation: Strong documentary proof exists, including an official technician job sheet confirming the manufacturing hardware defect within the timeline.

escalation_check.legal_aid_contact: District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Toll-Free Helpline: 15100

rights_advice.plain_language_standing:
You are well-protected under Indian consumer protection laws as a rightful buyer who received a defective product. Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, refusing to refund or replace defective goods within a reasonable period is considered an unfair trade practice. Your immediate takeaway is that you hold strong documentary proof, including a technician's job sheet, and can successfully seek redressal through consumer dispute forums without needing a lawyer initially.

As a consumer who bought a smartphone for personal use, you have full legal standing to seek a complete refund or replacement. The e-commerce platform and seller cannot arbitrarily hide behind internal return window policies when their own authorized technician officially verified the manufacturing defect.

governing_laws.relevance: Protects you as a consumer who bought goods for consideration.
Defines a 'defect' in goods, covering the hardware and screen issues you experienced.
Classifies refusing to refund or replace defective goods as an unfair trade practice.
Provides the legal basis for filing your consumer complaint electronically.

action_options.title: Immediate Pre-Litigation Action (Formal Legal Notice & Helpline)
action_options.details: Lodge an initial grievance on the National Consumer Helpline (NCH) via toll-free 1915 or consumerhelpline.gov.in. Simultaneously, serve a formal legal demand notice to the seller and e-commerce platform attaching your invoice and the technician's job sheet.

action_options.title: Statutory Authority / Grievance Portal Filing
action_options.details: File an electronic consumer complaint online on e-Jagriti with your order invoice, defect photos, technician job sheet, and chat history. Note: DLSA provides free legal aid and guidance only (Helpline 15100); it is never a forum for hearings or proceedings.

action_options.title: Statutory Forum / Consumer Commission Petition
action_options.details: If the platform fails to respond or resolve the issue following your notice and e-Jagriti filing, formally approach the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission with your complete evidence dossier.

rights_advice.real_lawyer_guidance: You can represent yourself comfortably in the Consumer Commission without hiring a physical advocate, as consumer forums are specifically designed for citizen self-representation. A lawyer is optional unless you prefer professional assistance for drafting documents.
rights_advice.disclaimer: ⚠️ NyayaMitra provides legal information and self-advocacy tools under Indian laws. For formal courtroom representation, consult a licensed advocate.

**SUBJECT: LEGAL DEMAND NOTICE FOR REFUND OF RS 26,999/- ALONG WITH COMPENSATION FOR SUPPLY OF DEFECTIVE SAMSUNG GALAXY SMARTPHONE AND UNFAIR TRADE PRACTICES UNDER THE CONSUMER PROTECTION ACT, 2019.**

Dear Sir/Madam,

I, am serving this legal demand notice upon you in my individual capacity as a consumer, to demand the immediate rectification of the grievance detailed herein.

### I hereby state and submit as under:

1. That on 10th November 2024, I ordered a Samsung Galaxy smartphone worth Rs 26,999 on your e-commerce platform under Order ID #[Insert Order ID].
2. That the said smartphone was delivered to my address on 14th November 2024.
3. That within 24 hours of opening the box, on 15th November 2024, the phone exhibited major functional defects as the screen started flickering and touch stopped working entirely. Consequently, I raised a replacement request on your application on the same day.
4. That on 21st November 2024, your e-commerce app technician visited my location, inspected the phone, officially confirmed the manufacturing hardware defect, and took my signature on his job sheet.
5. That despite your own authorized technician verifying the defect, your customer support arbitrarily cancelled my return request on 23rd November 2024, falsely stating that the 7-day return window had expired on 21st November 2024, and directed me to an authorized service center instead.
6. That supplying a defective product and subsequently refusing a replacement or refund despite internal verification constitutes a clear deficiency in service and an unfair trade practice under Section 2(10) and Section 2(47) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

### DEMAND FOR RECTIFICATION

In light of the above facts and statutory provisions under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, I hereby call upon you to:

1. Refund the full purchase amount of **Rs 26,999/-** immediately; OR
2. Provide a brand-new, defect-free replacement of the Samsung Galaxy smartphone as originally ordered, without imposing arbitrary conditions.

I suggest that you comply with the above demands within a **suggested 15-day period (customary pre-litigation practice)** from the date of receipt of this notice. 

*(Note: Under Section 84 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, liability applies strictly to the product manufacturer. E-commerce platforms and sellers remain liable for unfair trade practices and deficiencies in service as outlined above.)*

### WARNING

If you fail to comply with this notice within the suggested timeframe, I shall be constrained to initiate formal legal proceedings against you by filing an electronic consumer complaint on the e-Jagriti portal and subsequently before the competent District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, seeking a full refund, compensation for mental agony, and legal costs, at your sole risk, cost, and consequences.

---

### ANNEXURE INVENTORY:
1. Copy of Order Invoice
2. Delivery Receipt
3. Technician Inspection Job Sheet Copy
4. Screenshots of Chat with Customer Support

Sincerely / Yours faithfully,

*(Signature)* 
[Your Name]

sample_roleplay_turn.user_argument: Under Section 2(11) and Section 84 of the Consumer Protection Act 2019, delivering a defective phone and delaying inspection past your return window is a clear deficiency in service and unfair trade practice. I have the technician report confirming hardware fault. I demand an immediate refund or I will escalate to the National Consumer Helpline and e-Jagriti.

opponent_response.opponent_reply: Arre sir, why are you threatening with all these sections and Acts? Dekhiye, policy is policy. Technician report may be there, but our system says replacement window is strictly 7 days from delivery date, and it expired. We cannot bypass automated system rules for anyone. Maximum we can do is direct you to the authorized brand service center for repair. Refund is not possible at all.

coach_evaluation.what_went_well: You effectively cited the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (Sections 2(11) and 84) and presented the technician report as concrete proof.
coach_evaluation.what_to_improve: Reiterate the exact dates of delivery, technician visit, and cancellation to trap them in their own timeline contradiction.
coach_evaluation.suggested_next_counter: Your technician verified the hardware defect within the active window; refusing a replacement or refund for a defective product amounts to an unfair trade practice under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, and service center repair cannot replace my right to a defect-free product at delivery.
